Paragraph:
Translation: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.

Purport (Excerpt): The Lord says clearly that He Himself, Arjuna, and all the kings who are assembled on the battlefield, are eternally individual beings and that the Lord is eternally the maintainer of the individual living entities... Their individuality existed in the past, and their individuality will continue in the future without interruption. Therefore, there is no cause for lamentation for anyone.
Situation/Problem_Faced: Arjuna fears the permanent annihilation of his loved ones and himself through death in battle.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Krishna introduces the concept of eternal spiritual individuality. He guarantees that everyone present—Krishna, Arjuna, and all the soldiers—have always existed and will always exist as distinct individuals, entirely separate from their current physical forms.
Outcome/Resolution: This provides the absolute metaphysical counter-argument to the fear of death: death is merely an illusion, as the core identity never ceases to exist.

Mental_Health_Theme_Synonyms.identity Stability: A continuous sense of self across time

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Jiva-tattva (The philosophical truth regarding the individual living entity)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: This verse establishes the eternality of both the Supreme Lord and the individual souls. Krishna forcefully refutes the idea that individuality is a temporary product of material illusion. Because the soul is eternal and never ceases to exist, grieving over 'death' is illogical.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Krishna directly addresses Arjuna's existential anxiety and fear of death by providing a framework of absolute identity stability. By assuring Arjuna that the core 'self' is indestructible and continuous across past, present, and future, Krishna removes the rational basis for the terror of annihilation.
